hypotheses.reasoning: order-consumer is stuck on one message, msg-577362 at orders.events partition 1, offset 589882. Its payload contains a NUL byte at position 902, so JSON parsing fails every time (#1932, #2110, #2196, #2308). The consumer nacks and redelivers it with no max-retries configured (#1937 attempt 9, #2112 attempt 13), so the partition never advances. Normal batch processing stops after 05:46:42 (#1924 is the last batch), and lag then climbs from 606 messages at 05:48:45 (#2095) to 8124 at 05:55:28 (#2674). Consumer CPU stays normal because it is blocked on retries, not busy. The later order-service timeouts (#2252, #2397, #2653, #2820) are downstream effects of orders not being confirmed. The catalog-svc translation 401s (#1958, #2079, #2156, #2253) and the search-api/web-bff 502s are a separate incident on the search path and do not explain the orders.events backlog. Metrics-agent drops are also a side issue. Classification is poison_message rather than data_integrity because the fault is a single malformed record jamming the consumer, not a broad corruption or failed migration, though the NUL byte means the producer wrote bad data.

Alternative reading: the NUL byte means the order record was corrupted upstream, making this a data integrity problem at the producer. This would explain the bad payload, but the consumer-side jam is the direct cause of the lag, so poison_message is the better fit for the alert.

verdict.recommendedAction: Skip or quarantine msg-577362 (orders.events partition 1, offset 589882) to a dead-letter queue so the partition can advance. Add a max-retries limit with DLQ routing to order-consumer. Investigate the producer that wrote the NUL byte into the payload. Separately, rotate or fix the translation API key used by catalog-svc, which is returning 401s and causing the search 502s.
